findings.note: The canonical encoder this shard's new golden fixture pins can emit invalid JSON. internal/fsm/run/types.go:356 does bytes.ReplaceAll(out, []byte(`\ufffd`), []byte("\ufffd")) over the already-encoded document, so a payload whose text contains the six literal characters \ufffd (encoded by encoding/json as \\ufffd) has its trailing six bytes replaced, yielding \<U+FFFD> — an invalid escape that json.Unmarshal refuses. Verified by running a scratch test in the package: output {"k":"\<U+FFFD>"}, round trip fails with 'invalid escape sequence \\\xef'. This is not hypothetical input: types.go itself contains that literal, so recording a diff of this repo as a run payload writes an unparseable line into the run log and breaks chain verification. The fix is to escape only when the six bytes are a real JSON escape (operate on the encoder output as JSON, not as raw text). internal/fsm/run/golden_test.go, added in this shard, is billed as the R4 regression fixture for canonical form but its happyLog corpus contains no such payload, so the case is unpinned.

evidence.note: bytes.ReplaceAll over encoded JSON corrupts an escaped literal backslash

findings.note: golden_test.go fails badly rather than clearly on a drifted golden pair. The snapshot loop indexes stored[:i+1] while iterating the snapshots file, so a snapshots file with more lines than the log file panics with index out of range before the i != len(stored) guard is reached. Neither sc.Err() nor ws.Err() is checked, so a golden line over MaxLine (or a read error) silently shortens stored instead of failing the test — the same condition that then triggers the panic.

evidence.note: bufio.Scanner errors are never checked for either file

findings.note: The gate package doc claims RealExec runs git with 'config injection disabled', which overstates what it does. GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 suppresses only /etc/gitconfig; the user's global ~/.gitconfig is still read (GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL is scrubbed but never pointed at /dev/null), and only diff.external, core.excludesFile, core.attributesFile and core.fsmonitor are neutralised with -c. WorkTree's `git add -A` path can therefore still run filter.<driver>.clean commands configured globally or via a repo .gitattributes. Separately, WorkTree writes blob objects for every tracked and untracked file into the repository object store on each call — the scratch index is temporary but the objects it creates are not.

evidence.note: package doc says nothing here calls an LLM and config injection is disabled
RealExec -c list and env do not disable the global config file

findings.note: Cancellation is reported as a git failure rather than as cancellation. RealExec converts any *exec.ExitError into (code, nil), so a context-cancelled git returns code -1 with err nil; runEnv then sees code not in {0,1} and produces ERR_GIT 'git <op> exited -1' instead of surfacing ctx.Err(). asExit also uses a bare type assertion where errors.As would be the robust form.

evidence.note: ExitError is flattened to a code with err set to nil, losing the context error
asExit type-asserts instead of using errors.As
